29	# governed by a tenant policy (management is exempt from enforcement).
30	ACTION_POLICY_READ = "policy_read"
31	ACTION_POLICY_UPDATE = "policy_update"
32	ACTION_POLICY_DELETE = "policy_delete"
33	ACTIONS = (
34	    ACTION_CREATE,
35	    ACTION_READ,
36	    ACTION_ROTATE,
37	    ACTION_REVOKE,
38	    ACTION_IMPORT,
39	    ACTION_EXPORT,
40	    ACTION_AUDIT,
41	    ACTION_TENANT_CONFLICT,
42	    ACTION_POLICY_READ,
43	    ACTION_POLICY_UPDATE,
44	    ACTION_POLICY_DELETE,
45	)
46	
47	OUTCOME_SUCCESS = "success"
48	OUTCOME_REJECTED = "rejected"
49	OUTCOMES = (OUTCOME_SUCCESS, OUTCOME_REJECTED)
50	
51	_LOG_NAME = "audit.log"
52	_LOCK_NAME = "audit.log.lock"
53	_SECRET_NAME = "audit.secret"
54	
55	
56	class LedgerError(Exception):
57	    """Raised when the audit ledger cannot be written or read durably."""
58	
59	
60	class InvalidCursor(Exception):
61	    """Raised when a pagination cursor is malformed, tampered or stale."""
62	
63	
64	@dataclass
65	class AuditEvent:
66	    """One immutable audit record. Never carries key material."""
67	
68	    event_id: str
69	    tenant_id: Optional[str]
70	    action: str
71	    key_id: Optional[str]
72	    outcome: str
73	    timestamp: str
74	    seq: int = 0
75	
76	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
77	        """Serialize to a plain dict suitable for JSON storage."""
78	        return {
79	            "event_id": self.event_id,
80	            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
81	            "action": self.action,
82	            "key_id": self.key_id,
83	            "outcome": self.outcome,
84	            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
85	            "seq": self.seq,
86	        }
87	
88	    @classmethod
89	    def from_json(cls, data: dict) -> "AuditEvent":
90	        return cls(
91	            event_id=data["event_id"],
92	            tenant_id=data.get("tenant_id"),
93	            action=data["action"],
94	            key_id=data.get("key_id"),
95	            outcome=data["outcome"],
96	            timestamp=data["timestamp"],
97	            seq=int(data.get("seq", 0)),
98	        )
99	
100	    def to_response(self) -> dict:
101	        """Projection for GET /v1/audit: ledger-internal seq is omitted."""
102	        return {
103	            "event_id": self.event_id,
104	            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
105	            "action": self.action,
106	            "key_id": self.key_id,
107	            "outcome": self.outcome,
108	            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
109	        }
110	
111	
112	class AuditPage(NamedTuple):
113	    """Result of one ledger query: a page of events and the next cursor."""
114	
115	    events: List[AuditEvent]
116	    next_cursor: Optional[str]
117	
118	
119	class AuditLog:
120	    """File-backed append-only audit log (one JSON object per line).
121	
122	    All appends are serialized by one process-wide lock plus an exclusive
123	    ``fcntl`` lock on a sidecar file, so multiple server threads and processes
124	    share a monotonic ``seq`` without interleaving or losing lines. Pagination
125	    cursors are HMAC-signed and bound to the tenant, the active filters and the
126	    ledger snapshot they were issued against.
127	    """
128	
129	    def __init__(self, data_dir: str) -> None:
130	        self.data_dir = data_dir
131	        os.makedirs(self.data_dir, exist_ok=True)
132	        self._log_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOG_NAME)
133	        self._lock_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOCK_NAME)
134	        self._secret_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _SECRET_NAME)
135	        self._append_lock = threading.Lock()
136	        self._secret: Optional[bytes] = None
137	
138	    # -- paths / locking ---------------------------------------------------
139	    @property
140	    def path(self) -> str:
141	        return self._log_path
142	
143	    def _locked_file(self):
144	        """Open the sidecar lock file and take an exclusive fcntl lock."""
145	        fd = os.open(self._lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
146	        if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
147	            return fd
148	        try:
149	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
150	        except OSError:
151	            os.close(fd)
152	            raise
153	        return fd
154	
155	    def _unlock_file(self, fd: int) -> None:
156	        try:
157	            if fcntl is not None:  # pragma: no branch - POSIX in practice
158	                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
159	        finally:
160	            os.close(fd)
161	
162	    def _signing_secret(self) -> bytes:
163	        """Load (creating once, 0600) the HMAC secret used for cursors.
164	
165	        The read-or-create runs under the same cross-process file lock as
166	        appends, so two processes initializing concurrently cannot raise
167	        FileExistsError or read a half-written secret.
168	        """
169	        if self._secret is not None:
170	            return self._secret
171	        try:
172	            with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
173	                secret = fh.read()
174	            if secret:
175	                self._secret = secret
176	                return secret
177	        except FileNotFoundError:
178	            pass
179	        fd = self._locked_file()
180	        try:
181	            # Re-check under the lock: another process may have completed
182	            # the initialization while this one waited.
183	            try:
184	                with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
185	                    secret = fh.read()
186	                if secret:
187	                    self._secret = secret
188	                    return secret
189	            except FileNotFoundError:
190	                pass
191	            secret = os.urandom(32).hex().encode("ascii")
192	            out = os.open(
193	                self._secret_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600
194	            )
195	            try:
196	                os.write(out, secret)
197	                os.fsync(out)
198	            finally:
199	                os.close(out)
200	            self._secret = secret
201	            return secret
202	        finally:
203	            self._unlock_file(fd)
204	
205	    # -- reads -------------------------------------------------------------
206	    def _read_all_locked(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
207	        """Read every ledger line. Caller must hold no lock; takes none."""
208	        try:
209	            with open(self._log_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
210	                lines = fh.readlines()
211	        except FileNotFoundError:
212	            return []
213	        except OSError as exc:
214	            raise LedgerError("cannot read audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
215	        events: List[AuditEvent] = []
216	        for line in lines:
217	            line = line.strip()
218	            if not line:
219	                continue
220	            try:
221	                events.append(AuditEvent.from_json(json.loads(line)))
222	            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
223	                # A torn/corrupt tail line must not poison reads; the writer
224	                # only ever fsyncs complete lines.
225	                continue
226	        return events
227	
228	    def _read_all(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
229	        """Read under both locks for a consistent cross-process snapshot.
230	
231	        Appends commit (write + fsync) while holding the exclusive file
232	        lock, so a reader holding the same lock never observes a torn or
233	        partially-committed tail.
234	        """
235	        with self._append_lock:
236	            fd = self._locked_file()
237	            try:
238	                return self._read_all_locked()
239	            finally:
240	                self._unlock_file(fd)
241	
242	    @staticmethod
243	    def _fingerprint(events: List[AuditEvent]) -> str:
244	        """Stable digest identifying one ledger snapshot (its event set)."""
245	        digest = hashlib.sha256()
246	        for event in events:
247	            digest.update(str(event.seq).encode("ascii"))
248	            digest.update(b":")
249	            digest.update(event.event_id.encode("utf-8"))
250	            digest.update(b"\n")
251	        digest.update(b"count=%d" % len(events))
252	        return digest.hexdigest()
253	
254	    # -- writes ------------------------------------------------------------
255	    def new_event(
256	        self,
257	        tenant_id: Optional[str],
258	        action: str,
259	        key_id: Optional[str],
260	        outcome: str,
261	        timestamp: Optional[str] = None,
262	    ) -> AuditEvent:
263	        """Mint an event with a fresh event_id and UTC timestamp (seq unset)."""
264	        # Imported lazily to avoid a module import cycle at package import.
265	        from datetime import datetime, timezone
266	
267	        return AuditEvent(
268	            event_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
269	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
270	            action=action,
271	            key_id=key_id,
272	            outcome=outcome,
273	            timestamp=timestamp
274	            or datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
275	        )
276	
277	    def append(self, event: AuditEvent) -> AuditEvent:
278	        """Append one event durably, assigning the next monotonic seq.
279	
280	        Raises LedgerError if the line cannot be committed. The fsync before
281	        release means a returned event is on disk.
282	        """
283	        with self._append_lock:
284	            fd = self._locked_file()
285	            try:
286	                existing = self._read_all_locked()
287	                # Idempotent on event_id: recovery re-append after a crash
288	                # between the ledger write and the outbox-marker clear must
289	                # not produce a duplicate line.
290	                for prior in existing:
291	                    if prior.event_id == event.event_id:
292	                        event.seq = prior.seq
293	                        return event
294	                event.seq = (existing[-1].seq + 1) if existing else 1
295	                line = json.dumps(event.to_json(), separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
296	                try:
297	                    with open(self._log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
298	                        fh.write(line)
299	                        fh.flush()
300	                        os.fsync(fh.fileno())
301	                except OSError as exc:
302	                    raise LedgerError("cannot write audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
303	            finally:
304	                self._unlock_file(fd)
305	        return event
306	
307	    def get_event(self, event_id: str) -> Optional[AuditEvent]:
308	        """Look up one event by event_id, or None if it has not been logged.
309	
310	        Used by multi-file restore recovery to decide whether the shared
311	        event reached the ledger after a crash.
312	        """
313	        for event in self._read_all():
314	            if event.event_id == event_id:
315	                return event
316	        return None
317	
318	    # -- cursors -----------------------------------------------------------
319	    def _encode_cursor(self, payload: dict) -> str:
320	        raw = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
321	        token = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=")
322	        mac = hmac.new(self._signing_secret(), token, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
323	        return (token + b"." + mac.encode("ascii")).decode("ascii")
324	
325	    def _decode_cursor(self, raw: str) -> dict:
326	        try:
327	            token_b, mac_b = raw.encode("ascii").split(b".", 1)
328	        except (ValueError, AttributeError) as exc:
329	            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
330	        expected = hmac.new(
331	            self._signing_secret(), token_b, hashlib.sha256
332	        ).hexdigest().encode("ascii")
333	        if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, mac_b):
334	            raise InvalidCursor("invalid or tampered cursor")
335	        padded = token_b + b"=" * (-len(token_b) % 4)
336	        try:
337	            payload = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(padded).decode("utf-8"))
338	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
339	            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
340	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
341	            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor")
342	        return payload
343	
344	    # -- queries -----------------------------------------------------------
345	    @staticmethod
346	    def _sort_key(event: AuditEvent):
347	        return event.timestamp, event.event_id, event.seq
348	
349	    def query(
350	        self,
351	        tenant_id: str,
352	        key_id: Optional[str] = None,
353	        action: Optional[str] = None,
354	        limit: int = 100,
355	        cursor: Optional[str] = None,
356	    ) -> AuditPage:
357	        """Return one tenant-isolated, filter-bound, snapshot-bound page.
358	
359	        Events are ordered by (timestamp, event_id) ascending. Conflict
360	        records carry a null tenant and are therefore visible to nobody.
361	        A cursor is valid only with the same tenant, filters and an unchanged
362	        ledger snapshot; otherwise InvalidCursor is raised.
363	        """
364	        anchor = None
365	        fingerprint = None
366	        if cursor is not None:
367	            payload = self._decode_cursor(cursor)
368	            try:
369	                if payload.get("t") != tenant_id:
370	                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match tenant_id")
371	                if payload.get("k") != key_id or payload.get("a") != action:
372	                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match filters")
373	                if int(payload.get("l", -1)) != limit:
374	                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match limit")
375	                anchor = (payload["ts"], payload["eid"], int(payload["seq"]))
376	                fingerprint = payload["f"]
377	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
378	                raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
379	
380	        events = self._read_all()
381	
382	        selected_all = [
383	            e
384	            for e in events
385	            if e.tenant_id == tenant_id
386	            and (key_id is None or e.key_id == key_id)
387	            and (action is None or e.action == action)
388	        ]
389	        selected_all.sort(key=self._sort_key)
390	        # The snapshot is scoped to exactly the events this tenant and these
391	        # filters can see: another tenant's activity must not invalidate the
392	        # cursor, while any change to the visible set does.
393	        current_fingerprint = self._fingerprint(selected_all)
394	        if fingerprint is not None and fingerprint != current_fingerprint:
395	            raise InvalidCursor("cursor snapshot is no longer valid")
396	
397	        selected = selected_all
398	        if anchor is not None:
399	            selected = [e for e in selected if self._sort_key(e) > anchor]
400	
401	        page = selected[:limit]
402	        if len(selected) > limit and page:
403	            last = page[-1]
404	            next_cursor = self._encode_cursor(
405	                {
406	                    "v": 1,
407	                    "t": tenant_id,
408	                    "k": key_id,
409	                    "a": action,
410	                    "l": limit,
411	                    "ts": last.timestamp,
412	                    "eid": last.event_id,
413	                    "seq": last.seq,
414	                    "f": current_fingerprint,
415	                }
416	            )
417	        else:
418	            next_cursor = None
419	        return AuditPage(events=page, next_cursor=next_cursor)
420

"""Persistent append-only audit ledger with tenant-isolated pagination."""

import base64
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import os
import threading
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, NamedTuple, Optional

try:  # fcntl is POSIX-only.
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
    fcntl = None

# Actions written to the ledger. A request with a missing, empty, illegal or
# tenant-inconsistent identifier is recorded as TENANT_CONFLICT instead.
ACTION_CREATE = "create"
ACTION_READ = "read"
ACTION_ROTATE = "rotate"
ACTION_REVOKE = "revoke"
ACTION_IMPORT = "import"
ACTION_EXPORT = "export"
ACTION_AUDIT = "audit"
ACTION_TENANT_CONFLICT = "tenant_conflict"
# Policy management actions. These are audited but are never themselves
# governed by a tenant policy (management is exempt from enforcement).
ACTION_POLICY_READ = "policy_read"
ACTION_POLICY_UPDATE = "policy_update"
ACTION_POLICY_DELETE = "policy_delete"
ACTIONS = (
    ACTION_CREATE,
    ACTION_READ,
    ACTION_ROTATE,
    ACTION_REVOKE,
    ACTION_IMPORT,
    ACTION_EXPORT,
    ACTION_AUDIT,
    ACTION_TENANT_CONFLICT,
    ACTION_POLICY_READ,
    ACTION_POLICY_UPDATE,
    ACTION_POLICY_DELETE,
)

OUTCOME_SUCCESS = "success"
OUTCOME_REJECTED = "rejected"
OUTCOMES = (OUTCOME_SUCCESS, OUTCOME_REJECTED)

_LOG_NAME = "audit.log"
_LOCK_NAME = "audit.log.lock"
_SECRET_NAME = "audit.secret"


class LedgerError(Exception):
    """Raised when the audit ledger cannot be written or read durably."""


class InvalidCursor(Exception):
    """Raised when a pagination cursor is malformed, tampered or stale."""


@dataclass
class AuditEvent:
    """One immutable audit record. Never carries key material."""

    event_id: str
    tenant_id: Optional[str]
    action: str
    key_id: Optional[str]
    outcome: str
    timestamp: str
    seq: int = 0

    def to_json(self) -> dict:
        """Serialize to a plain dict suitable for JSON storage."""
        return {
            "event_id": self.event_id,
            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
            "action": self.action,
            "key_id": self.key_id,
            "outcome": self.outcome,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "seq": self.seq,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, data: dict) -> "AuditEvent":
        return cls(
            event_id=data["event_id"],
            tenant_id=data.get("tenant_id"),
            action=data["action"],
            key_id=data.get("key_id"),
            outcome=data["outcome"],
            timestamp=data["timestamp"],
            seq=int(data.get("seq", 0)),
        )

    def to_response(self) -> dict:
        """Projection for GET /v1/audit: ledger-internal seq is omitted."""
        return {
            "event_id": self.event_id,
            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
            "action": self.action,
            "key_id": self.key_id,
            "outcome": self.outcome,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
        }


class AuditPage(NamedTuple):
    """Result of one ledger query: a page of events and the next cursor."""

    events: List[AuditEvent]
    next_cursor: Optional[str]


class AuditLog:
    """File-backed append-only audit log (one JSON object per line).

    All appends are serialized by one process-wide lock plus an exclusive
    ``fcntl`` lock on a sidecar file, so multiple server threads and processes
    share a monotonic ``seq`` without interleaving or losing lines. Pagination
    cursors are HMAC-signed and bound to the tenant, the active filters and the
    ledger snapshot they were issued against.
    """

    def __init__(self, data_dir: str) -> None:
        self.data_dir = data_dir
        os.makedirs(self.data_dir, exist_ok=True)
        self._log_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOG_NAME)
        self._lock_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOCK_NAME)
        self._secret_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _SECRET_NAME)
        self._append_lock = threading.Lock()
        self._secret: Optional[bytes] = None

    # -- paths / locking ---------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def path(self) -> str:
        return self._log_path

    def _locked_file(self):
        """Open the sidecar lock file and take an exclusive fcntl lock."""
        fd = os.open(self._lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
        if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
            return fd
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        except OSError:
            os.close(fd)
            raise
        return fd

    def _unlock_file(self, fd: int) -> None:
        try:
            if fcntl is not None:  # pragma: no branch - POSIX in practice
                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)

    def _signing_secret(self) -> bytes:
        """Load (creating once, 0600) the HMAC secret used for cursors.

        The read-or-create runs under the same cross-process file lock as
        appends, so two processes initializing concurrently cannot raise
        FileExistsError or read a half-written secret.
        """
        if self._secret is not None:
            return self._secret
        try:
            with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
                secret = fh.read()
            if secret:
                self._secret = secret
                return secret
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
        fd = self._locked_file()
        try:
            # Re-check under the lock: another process may have completed
            # the initialization while this one waited.
            try:
                with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
                    secret = fh.read()
                if secret:
                    self._secret = secret
                    return secret
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
            secret = os.urandom(32).hex().encode("ascii")
            out = os.open(
                self._secret_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600
            )
            try:
                os.write(out, secret)
                os.fsync(out)
            finally:
                os.close(out)
            self._secret = secret
            return secret
        finally:
            self._unlock_file(fd)

    # -- reads -------------------------------------------------------------
    def _read_all_locked(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
        """Read every ledger line. Caller must hold no lock; takes none."""
        try:
            with open(self._log_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                lines = fh.readlines()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return []
        except OSError as exc:
            raise LedgerError("cannot read audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
        events: List[AuditEvent] = []
        for line in lines:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                events.append(AuditEvent.from_json(json.loads(line)))
            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
                # A torn/corrupt tail line must not poison reads; the writer
                # only ever fsyncs complete lines.
                continue
        return events

    def _read_all(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
        """Read under both locks for a consistent cross-process snapshot.

        Appends commit (write + fsync) while holding the exclusive file
        lock, so a reader holding the same lock never observes a torn or
        partially-committed tail.
        """
        with self._append_lock:
            fd = self._locked_file()
            try:
                return self._read_all_locked()
            finally:
                self._unlock_file(fd)

    @staticmethod
    def _fingerprint(events: List[AuditEvent]) -> str:
        """Stable digest identifying one ledger snapshot (its event set)."""
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        for event in events:
            digest.update(str(event.seq).encode("ascii"))
            digest.update(b":")
            digest.update(event.event_id.encode("utf-8"))
            digest.update(b"\n")
        digest.update(b"count=%d" % len(events))
        return digest.hexdigest()

    # -- writes ------------------------------------------------------------
    def new_event(
        self,
        tenant_id: Optional[str],
        action: str,
        key_id: Optional[str],
        outcome: str,
        timestamp: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> AuditEvent:
        """Mint an event with a fresh event_id and UTC timestamp (seq unset)."""
        # Imported lazily to avoid a module import cycle at package import.
        from datetime import datetime, timezone

        return AuditEvent(
            event_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            action=action,
            key_id=key_id,
            outcome=outcome,
            timestamp=timestamp
            or datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        )

    def append(self, event: AuditEvent) -> AuditEvent:
        """Append one event durably, assigning the next monotonic seq.

        Raises LedgerError if the line cannot be committed. The fsync before
        release means a returned event is on disk.
        """
        with self._append_lock:
            fd = self._locked_file()
            try:
                existing = self._read_all_locked()
                # Idempotent on event_id: recovery re-append after a crash
                # between the ledger write and the outbox-marker clear must
                # not produce a duplicate line.
                for prior in existing:
                    if prior.event_id == event.event_id:
                        event.seq = prior.seq
                        return event
                event.seq = (existing[-1].seq + 1) if existing else 1
                line = json.dumps(event.to_json(), separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
                try:
                    with open(self._log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                        fh.write(line)
                        fh.flush()
                        os.fsync(fh.fileno())
                except OSError as exc:
                    raise LedgerError("cannot write audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
            finally:
                self._unlock_file(fd)
        return event

    def get_event(self, event_id: str) -> Optional[AuditEvent]:
        """Look up one event by event_id, or None if it has not been logged.

        Used by multi-file restore recovery to decide whether the shared
        event reached the ledger after a crash.
        """
        for event in self._read_all():
            if event.event_id == event_id:
                return event
        return None

    # -- cursors -----------------------------------------------------------
    def _encode_cursor(self, payload: dict) -> str:
        raw = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
        token = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=")
        mac = hmac.new(self._signing_secret(), token, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
        return (token + b"." + mac.encode("ascii")).decode("ascii")

    def _decode_cursor(self, raw: str) -> dict:
        try:
            token_b, mac_b = raw.encode("ascii").split(b".", 1)
        except (ValueError, AttributeError) as exc:
            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
        expected = hmac.new(
            self._signing_secret(), token_b, hashlib.sha256
        ).hexdigest().encode("ascii")
        if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, mac_b):
            raise InvalidCursor("invalid or tampered cursor")
        padded = token_b + b"=" * (-len(token_b) % 4)
        try:
            payload = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(padded).decode("utf-8"))
        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor")
        return payload

    # -- queries -----------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _sort_key(event: AuditEvent):
        return event.timestamp, event.event_id, event.seq

    def query(
        self,
        tenant_id: str,
        key_id: Optional[str] = None,
        action: Optional[str] = None,
        limit: int = 100,
        cursor: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> AuditPage:
        """Return one tenant-isolated, filter-bound, snapshot-bound page.

        Events are ordered by (timestamp, event_id) ascending. Conflict
        records carry a null tenant and are therefore visible to nobody.
        A cursor is valid only with the same tenant, filters and an unchanged
        ledger snapshot; otherwise InvalidCursor is raised.
        """
        anchor = None
        fingerprint = None
        if cursor is not None:
            payload = self._decode_cursor(cursor)
            try:
                if payload.get("t") != tenant_id:
                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match tenant_id")
                if payload.get("k") != key_id or payload.get("a") != action:
                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match filters")
                if int(payload.get("l", -1)) != limit:
                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match limit")
                anchor = (payload["ts"], payload["eid"], int(payload["seq"]))
                fingerprint = payload["f"]
            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
                raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc

        events = self._read_all()

        selected_all = [
            e
            for e in events
            if e.tenant_id == tenant_id
            and (key_id is None or e.key_id == key_id)
            and (action is None or e.action == action)
        ]
        selected_all.sort(key=self._sort_key)
        # The snapshot is scoped to exactly the events this tenant and these
        # filters can see: another tenant's activity must not invalidate the
        # cursor, while any change to the visible set does.
        current_fingerprint = self._fingerprint(selected_all)
        if fingerprint is not None and fingerprint != current_fingerprint:
            raise InvalidCursor("cursor snapshot is no longer valid")

        selected = selected_all
        if anchor is not None:
            selected = [e for e in selected if self._sort_key(e) > anchor]

        page = selected[:limit]
        if len(selected) > limit and page:
            last = page[-1]
            next_cursor = self._encode_cursor(
                {
                    "v": 1,
                    "t": tenant_id,
                    "k": key_id,
                    "a": action,
                    "l": limit,
                    "ts": last.timestamp,
                    "eid": last.event_id,
                    "seq": last.seq,
                    "f": current_fingerprint,
                }
            )
        else:
            next_cursor = None
        return AuditPage(events=page, next_cursor=next_cursor)

539	        def _import_key(self, parts, operator: str) -> None:
540	            """POST /v1/keys/import.
541	
542	            Decryption/tamper/format errors are 400s naming passphrase or
543	            bundle and never touch disk. A key_id the tenant already owns is
544	            a 409 that leaves the original record untouched; the same key_id
545	            owned by another tenant answers 404 so existence never leaks
546	            across tenants.
547	            """
548	            payload = self._read_json_object()
549	            if payload is None:
550	                return
551	            body_tenant = payload.get("tenant_id")
552	            if not isinstance(body_tenant, str) or not body_tenant:
553	                if not self._record_conflict():
554	                    return
555	                self._bad_request("field tenant_id must be a non-empty string")
556	                return
557	            tenant_id = self._tenant(parts, payload)
558	            if tenant_id is None:
559	                return
560	            passphrase = payload.get("passphrase")
561	            if not isinstance(passphrase, str) or not passphrase:
562	                if not self._record_attempt(
563	                    tenant_id, None, audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT,
564	                    audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED,
565	                ):
566	                    return
567	                self._bad_request(
568	                    "field passphrase must be a non-empty string"
569	                )
570	                return
571	            bundle = payload.get("bundle")
572	            if not isinstance(bundle, str) or not bundle:
573	                if not self._record_attempt(
574	                    tenant_id, None, audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT,
575	                    audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED,
576	                ):
577	                    return
578	                self._bad_request("field bundle must be a non-empty string")
579	                return
580	            try:
581	                decoded = keybundle.decode_bundle(bundle, passphrase)
582	            except keybundle.WrongPassphrase as exc:
583	                if not self._record_attempt(

585	                    audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED,
586	                ):
587	                    return
588	                self._bad_request(str(exc))
589	                return
590	            except keybundle.InvalidBundle as exc:
591	                if not self._record_attempt(
592	                    tenant_id, None, audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT,
593	                    audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED,
594	                ):
595	                    return
596	                self._bad_request(str(exc))
597	                return
598	            # The bundle authenticated; authorization now, before the
599	            # existence conflict check (deny is a 403 even when the key_id
600	            # already exists for another tenant).
601	            if not self._enforce(
602	                tenant_id, decoded["key_id"], audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT, operator
603	            ):
604	                return
605	            # The bundle authenticated; its key_id is a validated UUID4. The
606	            # existence check and the create happen atomically in the store.
607	            try:
608	                status, record = store.import_bundle(tenant_id, decoded)
609	            except ProviderInvalidMaterial as exc:
610	                # The sealed bundle was authentic but its material fails the
611	                # provider's algorithm checks: a 400 rejected import.
612	                if not self._record_attempt(
613	                    tenant_id, decoded["key_id"], audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT,
614	                    audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED,
615	                ):
616	                    return
617	                self._send_json(400, {"error": str(exc)})
618	                return
619	            if status == IMPORT_CONFLICT:
620	                if not self._record_attempt(
621	                    tenant_id, record.key_id, audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT,
622	                    audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED,
623	                ):
624	                    return
625	                if record.tenant_id == tenant_id:
626	                    self._send_json(
627	                        409, {"error": "key_id already exists for this tenant"}
628	                    )
629	                else:
630	                    # Same answer as a missing key: never confirm another
631	                    # tenant owns this key_id.
632	                    self._send_json(404, {"error": "key not found"})
633	                return
634	            # The success event committed in the same transaction as the file.
635	            self._send_json(201, record.to_create_response())

1	"""Cryptographic key generation for supported algorithms."""
2	
3	import base64
4	import os
5	from typing import NamedTuple, Optional
6	
7	from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
8	from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa
9	
10	SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS = ("AES256", "RSA2048")
11	
12	
13	class GeneratedKey(NamedTuple):
14	    """Result of generating a key.
15	
16	    public_material is PEM (SubjectPublicKeyInfo) for RSA, None for AES.
17	    private_material stays server-side only (PEM for RSA, base64 for AES).
18	    """
19	
20	    public_material: Optional[str]
21	    private_material: str
22	
23	
24	def _generate_aes256() -> GeneratedKey:
25	    """Generate a 256-bit AES key (no public component)."""
26	    raw = os.urandom(32)
27	    return GeneratedKey(
28	        public_material=None,
29	        private_material=base64.b64encode(raw).decode("ascii"),
30	    )
31	
32	
33	def _generate_rsa2048() -> GeneratedKey:
34	    """Generate a 2048-bit RSA key pair."""
35	    private_key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)
36	    private_pem = private_key.private_bytes(
37	        encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,
38	        format=serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
39	        encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),
40	    ).decode("ascii")
41	    public_pem = private_key.public_key().public_bytes(
42	        encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,
43	        format=serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo,
44	    ).decode("ascii")
45	    return GeneratedKey(
46	        public_material=public_pem,
47	        private_material=private_pem,
48	    )
49	
50	
51	def generate_key(algorithm: str) -> GeneratedKey:
52	    """Generate a new key for the given algorithm name."""
53	    if algorithm == "AES256":
54	        return _generate_aes256()
55	    if algorithm == "RSA2048":
56	        return _generate_rsa2048()
57	    raise ValueError("unsupported algorithm: %r" % (algorithm,))

def export_bundle(
        self, key_id: str, tenant_id: str, passphrase: str
    ) -> Optional[str]:
        """Seal a tenant's full key record into an opaque bundle.

        Returns None for an unknown or foreign key, so the caller cannot tell
        the two cases apart. Export does not mutate ordinary state, but a key
        still carrying raw pre-provider versions is adopted into the local
        provider here — lazily and atomically, and only when local is active.
        The adoption and the provider reads run under the key's locks so a
        concurrent rotation cannot interleave with the snapshot. Its audit
        event is appended by the caller alongside the response, like a read.
        """
        if not _KEY_ID_RE.fullmatch(key_id):
            return None
        path = self._path_for(key_id)
        with self._key_lock(key_id), self._file_lock(key_id):
            record = self._read_record(path)
            if record is None or record.tenant_id != tenant_id:
                return None
            self._adopt_legacy_versions_locked(path, record)
            return keybundle.encode_bundle(
                self.export_payload(record), passphrase
            )

        malformed material ProviderInvalidMaterial -> 400). A successful
        import and its audit event commit through the same outbox transaction
        as create/rotate, and a failure deletes every minted handle.
        """
        key_id = payload["key_id"]
        path = self._path_for(key_id)

        # locked conflict re-check below releases its handles.
        adopted = []  # (provider, handle)
        try:
            versions = []

            operator=payload["operator"],
            revoked_at=payload["revoked_at"],

        event = self.audit.new_event(
            tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT, key_id,
            audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS,
        )
        with self._key_lock(key_id), self._file_lock(key_id):
            # Phase B: conflict re-check under the locks; delete everything
            # this attempt minted and leave the existing record byte-for-byte

            if existing is not None:

        print("PASS:", name)
    else:
        FAILS.append((name, detail))
        print("FAIL:", name, detail)


def fresh_dir(name):
    d = os.path.join(KM, "data-" + name)
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(d)
    return d


def env_for(data_dir, provider=None, extra=None):
    e = dict(os.environ)
    e["PYTHONPATH"] = KM + ":" + ROOT
    e.pop("KEYMGR_PROVIDER", None)
    if provider:
        e["KEYMGR_PROVIDER"] = provider
    e["FAKEKMS_SENTINEL"] = os.path.join(data_dir, "fake-loaded")
    e["FAKEKMS_LOAD"] = "ok"
    e.pop("FAKEKMS_FAIL", None)
    if extra:
        e.update(extra)
    return e


def cli(data_dir, *args, provider=None, extra=None):
    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "keymgr", "--data-dir", data_dir] + list(args)
    p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True,
                       env=env_for(data_dir, provider, extra))
    return p.returncode, p.stdout.strip(), p.stderr.strip()


def wait_port(port, timeout=10):
    end = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < end:
        try:
            with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), 0.5):
                return True
        except OSError:
            time.sleep(0.1)
    return False


class Server:
    def __init__(self, data_dir, provider=None, extra=None):
        self.data_dir = data_dir
        # find a free port
        s = socket.socket()
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        self.port = s.getsockname()[1]
        s.close()
        self.proc = subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "keymgr", "--data-dir", data_dir,
             "serve", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", str(self.port)],
            env=env_for(data_dir, provider, extra),
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        )
        if not wait_port(self.port):
            out, err = self.proc.communicate(timeout=5)
            raise RuntimeError("server didn't start: " + err.decode())

    def stop(self):
        self.proc.terminate()
        try:
            self.proc.wait(timeout=5)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            self.proc.kill()

    def req(self, method, path, body=None, tenant=None, operator="alice"):
        url = "http://127.0.0.1:%d%s" % (self.port, path)
        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
        r = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method)
        if data is not None:
            r.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        if tenant is not None:
            r.add_header("X-Tenant-Id", tenant)
        r.add_header("X-Operator-Id", operator)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(r) as resp:
                return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read().decode() or "{}")
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            return e.code, json.loads(e.read().decode() or "{}")


def sentinel_loaded(data_dir):
    return os.path.exists(os.path.join(data_dir, "fake-loaded"))


def write_legacy_key_file(data_dir, key_id, tenant="ta", algorithm="AES256"):
    """Hand-write a pre-provider record carrying raw private_material."""
    g = generate_key(algorithm)
    flat = {
        "key_id": key_id,
        "tenant_id": tenant,
        "label": "legacy",
        "current_version": 1,
        "versions": [
            {
                "version": 1,
                "created_at": "2020-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
                "algorithm": algorithm,
                "public_key": g.public_material,
                "private_material": g.private_material,
            }
        ],
    }
    with open(os.path.join(data_dir, key_id + ".json"), "w") as fh:
        json.dump(flat, fh)
    return g.private_material


def strip_provider_blocks(payload):
    p = json.loads(json.dumps(payload))
    for v in p["versions"]:
        v.pop("provider", None)
    return p


def seal_legacy_key(payload, passphrase):
    return kb.seal_envelope(strip_provider_blocks(payload), passphrase, kb.FORMAT)

"""End-to-end black-box checks for the pluggable KMS/HSM fixes.

Runs the real CLI and a real `python -m keymgr serve` subprocess, switching
KEYMGR_PROVIDER between runs. Prints PASS/FAIL lines and exits non-zero on any
failure.
"""

import base64
import json
import os
import shutil
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
import urllib.error
import uuid
from http.client import RemoteDisconnected

ROOT = "/var/tmp/solo/task01/task010"
KM = "/var/tmp/solo/kmtest"
sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)
sys.path.insert(0, KM)

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa

from keymgr import keybundle as kb
from keymgr import tenantbundle as tb
from keymgr.crypto import generate_key

PASS, FAILS = 0, []


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    global PASS
    if cond:
        PASS += 1
        print("PASS:", name)
    else:
        FAILS.append((name, detail))
        print("FAIL:", name, detail)


def fresh_dir(name):
    d = os.path.join(KM, "data-" + name)
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(d)
    return d


def env_for(data_dir, provider=None, extra=None):
    e = dict(os.environ)
    e["PYTHONPATH"] = KM + ":" + ROOT
    e.pop("KEYMGR_PROVIDER", None)
    if provider:
        e["KEYMGR_PROVIDER"] = provider
    e["FAKEKMS_SENTINEL"] = os.path.join(data_dir, "fake-loaded")
    e["FAKEKMS_LOAD"] = "ok"
    e.pop("FAKEKMS_FAIL", None)
    if extra:
        e.update(extra)
    return e


def cli(data_dir, *args, provider=None, extra=None):
    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "keymgr", "--data-dir", data_dir] + list(args)
    p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True,
                       env=env_for(data_dir, provider, extra))
    return p.returncode, p.stdout.strip(), p.stderr.strip()


def wait_port(port, timeout=10):
    end = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < end:
        try:
            with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), 0.5):
                return True
        except OSError:
            time.sleep(0.1)
    return False


class Server:
    def __init__(self, data_dir, provider=None, extra=None):
        self.data_dir = data_dir
        # find a free port
        s = socket.socket()
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        self.port = s.getsockname()[1]
        s.close()
        self.proc = subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "keymgr", "--data-dir", data_dir,
             "serve", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", str(self.port)],
            env=env_for(data_dir, provider, extra),
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        )
        if not wait_port(self.port):
            out, err = self.proc.communicate(timeout=5)
            raise RuntimeError("server didn't start: " + err.decode())

    def stop(self):
        self.proc.terminate()
        try:
            self.proc.wait(timeout=5)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            self.proc.kill()

    def req(self, method, path, body=None, tenant=None, operator="alice"):
        url = "http://127.0.0.1:%d%s" % (self.port, path)
        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
        r = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method)
        if data is not None:
            r.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        if tenant is not None:
            r.add_header("X-Tenant-Id", tenant)
        r.add_header("X-Operator-Id", operator)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(r) as resp:
                return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read().decode() or "{}")
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            return e.code, json.loads(e.read().decode() or "{}")


def sentinel_loaded(data_dir):
    return os.path.exists(os.path.join(data_dir, "fake-loaded"))


def write_legacy_key_file(data_dir, key_id, tenant="ta", algorithm="AES256"):
    """Hand-write a pre-provider record carrying raw private_material."""
    g = generate_key(algorithm)

    }
    with open(os.path.join(data_dir, key_id + ".json"), "w") as fh:

    p = json.loads(json.dumps(payload))

content.description: _provider_for must require the record/block provider_id to match the ACTIVE provider instance (local only usable when local active); missing provider block on legacy bundles -> local, rejected (503) when active isn't local. Remove unconditional startup migration; add lazy atomic legacy-version adoption only when local is active and material is first needed (export/backup), preserving original file on failure. Normal reads must not load provider or rewrite files. Fix export locking, and _commit_mutation handle lifecycle (release handles only before commit point; never roll back/delete handles after durable audit append).

content.subject: Fix transaction cleanup: post-commit marker failures must not roll back or orphan handles
content.description: In restore.py phase 3 (marker clear after durable ledger append) and empty-restore finalize, failures must surface as LedgerError without deleting files/handles; restart recovery idempotently finishes. Verify pre-commit rollback deletes all minted handles. In cli.py map startup LedgerError/ProviderUnavailable to fixed exit codes.
